newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS WIN DRAFT LOTTERY.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-BRUINS WIN DRAFT LOTTERY.

text.p: The Boston Bruins finally won something -- Sunday's National Hockey League draft lottery.
Boston, which had the league's worst record during the regular season, won the first shot at top prospect Joe Thornton.
The bottom 10 teams in the league during the regular season -- the non-playoff teams -- all had a chance to win the drawing but Boston got the top pick.
Following Boston in the draft will be the San Jose Sharks and Los Angeles Kings.

The New York Islanders have their own pick in the fourth position as well as the Toronto Maple Leafs' selection at number five. The Calgary Flames pick next, followed by the Tampa Bay Lightning and Boston again with the former Hartford Whalers' slot.
Washington Capitals and Vancouver Canucks round out the first 10 choices.
The other 16 draft positions go in reverse order of teams' regular-season standings.
Thornton, a centre for the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds of the Ontario Hockey League, was the top draft prospect in the NHL Central Scouting final rankings released earlier this week.

The 6-4 (1.98 metres), 198-pound (60 km) Thornton, who will turn 18 on July 2, maintained the ranking he received at mid-season. He was second in points and assists in the OHL and was a second-team All-Star.

Centres Patrick Marleau of the Seattle Thunderbirds of the Western Hockey League and Daniel Tkaczuk of the Barrie Colts of the OHL ranked behind Thornton, while Roberto Luongo of the Val d'Or Foreurs of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League was rated the top North American goaltender.
